title: GA/252/2007 of STATE OF UTTARAKHAND Vs DHARMPAL

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT
NAINITAL
Government Appeal No. 252 of 2007

Versus
Dharmpal .......Respondents
Ms. Mamta Joshi, Brief Holder, for the State/appellant.
Mr. Sandeep Tandon, Advocate, for the respondents.
September 11, 2020

Hon'ble N.S. Dhanik, J.
Vide impugned judgment and order dated
16.4.2007, passed by the Additional Sessions
Judge/Special Judge, NDPS, Dehradun in SST No.
15/2005, the respondent Dharmpal was convicted for
the offence under Section 8/20 of the NDPS Act and
sentenced to undergo simple imprisonment of two years
three months and 16 days and to pay a fine of Rs.
20,000/-. On the date of pronouncement of order of
sentence, the accused had already undergone the jail
sentence imposed on him. Feeling aggrieved with the
quantum of sentence, the State has preferred the
present appeal.

I have heard learned Counsel for the parties
and perused the materials on record.
The main contention of the learned State
Counsel is that since approximately one and half
kilograms charas was recovered from the possession of
the accused respondent and such quantity being more
than commercial quantity, the convict was liable to be
sentenced with rigorous imprisonment for a term not
less than ten years but which may extend to twenty

2
years, as is provided under Section 20(b)(ii)(C) of the
NDPS Act.
Sri Sandeep Tandon, learned Counsel
appearing for the accused respondent refuted the
contention made on behalf of State and submitted that
the quantity of charas, allegedly recovered from the
accused respondent is itself doubtful and disputed.
Learned Counsel submitted that the evidence on record
would show that the charas recovered from the accused
respondent was never, in fact, weighed and an
approximate quantity of the contraband has been
mentioned by the prosecution everywhere. As such, it
cannot be said that the quantity of contraband was
more than commercial quantity and, therefore, the trial
court rightly imposed the punishment of jail sentence
in terms of the provision under Section 20(b)(ii)(B) of
the NDPS Act. Learned State Counsel also fairly
admitted that there is no evidence of weighing the
contraband.
Having perused the evidence on record, I
find that there is no material on record to show that the
contraband was weighed at any point of time. It was a
sudden recovery. Police party did not have any prior
information. There is no independent witness of the
recovery either. PW1, who was leading the patrolling
police party, admitted in his cross-examination that the
recovered contraband was not weighed in the police
station. In his examination-in-chief, PW1 has also
stated that he did not know as to how much exact
quantity was taken out for preparing the sample. PW2,
who was member of the police party, has also stated
that a tentative/approximate quantity of 100 grams
was taken out for preparing the sample. He further

3
admitted this fact in his cross-examination as well and
also stated that number of pieces of charas, taken out
for the sample, was not written. No other member of the
police party has been examined as witness in the trial
court. Even in the recovery memo, "approximately 1.5
Kg charas" has been mentioned.
In view of the above, it cannot be said that
the recovered quantity of charas was weighed. As such,
the quantity recovered was an unsure quantity and,
therefore, it cannot be said that it was more than
commercial quantity. Hence, I find no illegality or
infirmity in the order of sentence awarded by the trial
court.
For the reasons recorded above, I do not
find any illegality in the impugned judgment and order.
The trial court has rightly imposed the jail sentence on
the accused respondent. Consequently, the present
appeal preferred by the State is dismissed. Impugned
judgment and order is affirmed.
Let a copy of this judgment and order, along
with LCR, be sent to the trial court.
 (N.S. Dhanik, J.)
